mintAuthority.summary: JPYC v1 has one reviewed native issuance deployment on Ethereum: the non-upgradeable legacy ERC-20 exposes an owner-restricted mint(address,uint256) function, and the current owner EOA can mint arbitrary amounts. Polygon and Gnosis are bridge representations assessed under bridgeRouteRisk, not additional native issuance chains.

controls.label: JPYC v1 Ethereum owner/minter (EOA)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770969 (2026-08-16T23:38:47Z), storage slot 8 of 0x2370f9d504c7a6e775bf6e14b3f12846b594cd53 returned 0x94c2d94a786e1aaa07e95d084e88cd3a0680d152; eth_getCode returned no bytecode (EOA), totalSupply() was 1,300,000,000 JPYC, and both EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots were zero. The official JPYC v1 source defines owner-only mint(address,uint256) with no aggregate or economic cap, so this is the sole native issuance control.

review.evidence: The corrected native scope is Ethereum only. At Ethereum block 25770969, storage slot 8 of 0x2370f9d504c7a6e775bf6e14b3f12846b594cd53 returned EOA 0x94c2d94a786e1aaa07e95d084e88cd3a0680d152, which had empty code; the official JPYC v1 source exposes owner-only mint(address,uint256) with no aggregate, time-window, reserve, or economic cap, and totalSupply() was 1,300,000,000 JPYC. Polygon and Gnosis are mapped bridge representations whose destination mint, burn, escrow, messaging, upgrade, and validator controls are reviewed under bridgeRouteRisk and are excluded from native Mint Authority. The native economic annotations therefore remain concentrated-admin, unbounded, unknown reconciliation, and no supervision.
review.reviewer: Codex mint/bridge boundary migration; verified JPYC v1 finding
